en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Dharma Gate for Protecting Life, translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was beneath the Bodhi tree, having attained perfect enlightenment.
He was staying within a great caitya,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
among whom was the venerable Śāriputra.
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
the Venerable Ānanda,
and other such great śrāvakas served as their leaders.
He was together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas,
whose names were Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva and Vajragarbha Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and others such as these,
who were the leaders of the entire assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas within this Bhadrakalpa.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
we only pray that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha [will grant us his teaching]."
For the sake of all sentient beings, he expounded this subtle Dharma-gate for the protection of life. By means of this Dharma-gate,
he provides great illumination and great shelter for all sentient beings.
May those sentient beings attain fearlessness;
may all enemies, wicked associates,
whether gods, nāgas, or yakṣas, [be overcome].
Whether they be rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas,
or other humans and non-humans,
they shall ultimately be unable to give rise to evil intentions to cause disturbance or seize their vital essence.
If one encounters swords, blades, food, drink, or poisonous medicines,
or various afflictions resulting from incantations and curses, they shall be unable to cause harm.
Should there be sentient beings— whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down— [who encounter this, they shall likewise be protected].
Whether in sleep, in a state of intoxication, or in full wakefulness,
may I be able to protect [them] in all circumstances;
may the Blessed One grant this for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
Having thus proclaimed these various divine mantras,
[he said: "Just as I have always approached, served, and never departed from the presence of the Tathāgata,
so too shall I now protect all sentient beings."
For the sake of benefit, for the sake of peace and happiness,
and for the sake of welfare at all times, I now entreat the Tathāgata.
Protect all good men and good women who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle,
so that they may not be subjected to strife, quarreling, abuse, or disparagement, nor harbor resentment in their hearts.
Regarding all illnesses, sufferings, untimely deaths, and calamities,
after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi had thus made this request,
the Bhagavān addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, you have exhorted the Tathāgata.
Listen attentively now and reflect well upon it; I shall now expound for you the Dharma-door of Protecting Life.
It is named the "Gate of Goodness" (*Sugata*).

18. *Tā haridhañje*. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi:
O Bodhisattva,
this *dhāraṇī* mantra of the "Gate of Skillful Means for Protecting Life" was [taught] by the Tathāgatas,
Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past.
What was previously expounded has already been protected;
great vows have been made and truly established.
Now, for the benefit and out of compassion for all sentient beings, I likewise [act].
Having made great vows and established them with truth,
he therefore spoke this dhāraṇī mantra.
At that time, the Bhagavān emitted from the ūrṇā-kośa between his eyebrows a light of the marks of a Great Man.
That light shone universally throughout all Buddha-fields.
By the miraculous power of the Buddha, all Tathāgatas within those fields beheld this radiance and simultaneously set out from their respective lands for the Sahā world.
Arriving at the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was, he praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Buddha!
It is because you are able to benefit and protect all sentient beings."
I shall now proclaim this dharma-gate dhāraṇī-mantra,
which is able to produce radiance, bring about joy, and secure right mindfulness;
for this reason, I now extol and praise it.
If there are good men or good women who,
at the time of dawn, receive, uphold, read, and recite the words and meanings of this divine dhāraṇī mantra,
they shall obtain twenty kinds of merit.
First, they shall be taken into the care of all Buddhas;
second, they shall be constantly remembered by all Buddhas;
third, they shall forever be free from the karma that leads to rebirth in the evil realms.
Fourth, one shall obtain long life and wealth;
fifth, one shall obtain a reputation that is heard far and wide;
sixth, one shall obtain courageous power and majesty.
Seventh, they are constantly free from illness and are further able to practice with diligence.
Eighth, they are always protected by all the Buddhas.
Ninth, they are furthermore remembered by all the devas.
Tenth, one diligently cultivates wholesome conduct.
Eleventh, one shall attain radiant joy and right mindfulness.
Twelfth, one shall attain the perfection of all the marks.
Thirteenth, they shall attain fearlessness.
Fourteenth, they shall fully possess ethical discipline (*śīla*).
Fifteenth, they shall achieve all roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*).
Sixteenth, one shall receive the protection of the devas;
seventeenth, one shall receive the protection of the nāgas;
eighteenth, one shall receive the protection of the yakṣas.
Nineteenth, one shall be revered and loved by all the world.
Twentieth, one shall swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi:
"I shall now proclaim this dhāraṇī mantra;
it is the secret locus of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas."
It is protected by all the Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
I now also proclaim this dhāraṇī for the sake of protecting and benefiting all good sons and good daughters.
If there should be anyone who is able to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī mantra of the Dharma-gate for Protecting Life, [they shall be guarded].
"At the time of dawn, you should rise and engage in recitation.
World-Honored One, I shall constantly protect such persons as these, ensuring they are free from affliction and harm."

If one is able to receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī mantra of the Dharma-gate for Protecting Life at the time of dawn,
that person shall be [regarded] by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
It is protected by all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
When the Bhagavat had finished speaking this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
as well as Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, devas, asuras, gandharvas, and all the members of the assembly,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
